_comment: Tier-2 for skfem navier_stokes#1, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: the block system is [[A_visc + C(u), B^T],[B, 0]]; omitting C(u) leaves a Stokes Jacobian and Newton converges linearly with 'residual ratio ~0.5 per iteration' instead of geometrically. Ran: lid-driven cavity at Re=100, Taylor-Hood ElementVector(TriP2)/TriP1 on MeshTri().refined(3), one pressure DOF pinned, full Jacobian vs Jacobian with the convection block omitted, with the residual ALWAYS taken from the full Navier-Stokes equations so only the Jacobian differs. Printed: the ORDER claim is confirmed -- the full Jacobian falls 1.177e-02 / 1.484e-04 / 1.881e-09 / 1.605e-17 in 4 iterations (quadratic) while the Stokes Jacobian takes 15 at a constant ratio. THE QUOTED RATE IS WRONG in the safe-looking direction: the measured ratio settles near 0.17, not 0.5, so the inexact iteration converges considerably FASTER than the entry implies and a gate watching for 'ratio about 0.5' never fires. It still converges, silently, to the same solution to 1.071e-12 relative -- the defect costs iterations, not correctness, so only the ORDER reveals it and a single-tolerance run cannot. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 switches the second run's variant string 'defective' from 'stokes' (J = A) to 'newton' (J = A + C1 + C2), putting the omitted convection block C(u) back into the Jacobian -- the documented fix, applied at the Jacobian-assembly site. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 10 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 makes both runs converge in the same 4 iterations, which removes 'stokes_needs_more_iterations=True' and raises the forbidden 'FAIL:' ('FAIL: omitting C(u) cost no iterations'), so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
